narrative: For material PL3__MF5A1654, analysis of 228 working days reveals erratic demand with mean 1561 units/day and CV 0.62. Lead time is unstable (mean 1.10 days, CV 0.81). The recommended (r,Q) policy achieves a 95% service level with safety stock of 2,817 units (1.8 days coverage), reorder point of 4,528 units, and order quantity of 5,909 units reviewed every 4 days. This policy reduces annual costs by $150,776 (94.2%) compared to the current SAP micro-batch policy. Storage utilisation is at 100% of capacity and the dominant lead-time variance driver is transport (60%), making carrier reliability the primary lever for further safety-stock reduction.
warnings: Unstable lead time (CV=0.81). Consider supplier reliability improvements.
Order quantity constrained by storage capacity. EOQ=8756, OQ=5909.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic high-volume demand with a high ordering cost strongly favours large infrequent orders triggered by a fixed reorder point. The (r,Q) policy is the natural fit: the reorder point absorbs lead-time and demand variability via safety stock, while EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds at 100% utilisation post-replenishment (SS 2817 + OQ 5909 = 8726 = max_storage_units). Any concurrent demand spike and lead-time extension leaves zero headroom, increasing stockout risk beyond the 95% target.
